title: Analysis of Gapminder Dataset using R
text:
library(tidyverse)
library(gapminder)
This post uses the gapminder dataset to look at life expectancy across 142 different countries from 1952 to 2007
Data: Based on free material from GAPMINDER.ORG, CC-BY licence, via the gapminder R package.

title: Analysis of Gapminder Dataset using R
text:
Life Expectancy by continent
I took the averaged life expectancy across the countries in each continent for every survey year (1952-2007) to compare how life expectancy has changed in each continent.

continent_trend <- gapminder |>
  group_by(continent, year) |>
  summarise(mean_life = mean(lifeExp), .groups = "drop")

head(continent_trend)


  




ggplot(continent_trend, aes(year, mean_life, colour = continent)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Mean life expectancy (years)", colour = NULL) 







Figure 1: Mean life expectancy by continent, 1952–2007.





As Figure 1 shows that life expectancy has consistently been highest in Oceania, and lowest in Africa. Each continent has seen an increase in life expectancy between 1952 and 2007, with each continent’s life expectancy increasing monotonically except for Africa. There was a dip in life expectancy in Africa between the late 1990s and early 2000s before increasing again.

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from gapminder import gapminder
This post uses the gapminder dataset to look at life expectancy across 142 different countries from 1952 to 2007.
Data: Based on free material from GAPMINDER.ORG, CC-BY licence, from the gapminder Python package.

title: Analysis of Gapminder Dataset using Python
text:
Life Expectancy by continent
I took the averaged life expectancy across the countries in each continent for every survey year (1952–2007) to compare how life expectancy has changed in each continent.

continent_trend = (
    gapminder
    .groupby(["continent", "year"], as_index=False)
    .agg(mean_life=("lifeExp", "mean"))
)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 5))
for continent, group in continent_trend.groupby("continent"):
    ax.plot(group["year"], group["mean_life"], marker="o", linewidth=2,
            label=continent)
ax.set_ylabel("Mean life expectancy (years)")
ax.legend(frameon=False)
plt.show()







Figure 1: Mean life expectancy by continent, 1952–2007.





As Figure 1 shows, life expectancy has consistently been highest in Oceania (which in this dataset is only Australia and New Zealand) and lowest in Africa. Every continent’s life expectancy rose between 1952 and 2007, and all except Africa increased in every survey year. Africa’s average stalled from the late 1980s and dipped slightly between 1992 and 2002, before rising again by 2007.

title: Analysis of Gapminder Dataset using Python
text:
Which country gained the most?
Next I calculated the change in life expectancy for each country between 1952 and 2007.

life_change = (
    gapminder[gapminder["year"].isin([1952, 2007])]
    .pivot_table(index=["country", "continent"], columns="year",
                 values="lifeExp")
    .reset_index()
)
life_change.columns = ["country", "continent", "1952", "2007"]
life_change["change"] = life_change["2007"] - life_change["1952"]
life_change = life_change.sort_values("change", ascending=False,
                                      ignore_index=True)
 
n_declined = int((life_change["change"] < 0).sum())
top_country = life_change["country"].iloc[0]
top_change = f"{life_change['change'].iloc[0]:.1f}"
bottom_country = life_change["country"].iloc[-1]
bottom_change = f"{life_change['change'].iloc[-1]:.1f}"
